Lessons.Title: Using Quadratic Equations to Model Situations and Solve Problems
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: synthesize modeling, quadratic graphs, equation forms and exact solving in an open contextual investigation, including intersections of a parabola and a line, and justify all admissible results without step-by-step scaffolding. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 24 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/24/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/24/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source culminates in student-directed analysis rather than one rote factorization question.

Original fictitious simultaneous height comparison: a lightweight test object is modeled at height H(t)=−t²+6t+2 metres for elapsed t≥0 seconds until it reaches ground. A separately moving platform has height P(t)=t+6 metres under a simplified straight-line rule over the same time interval. Comparing elevations does not by itself establish a physical collision because horizontal positions and safety are not modeled.

Set H(t)=P(t) to find shared heights: −t²+6t+2=t+6, hence −t²+5t−4=0 or (t−1)(t−4)=0 after multiplying by−1. Thus t=1 or4 seconds; at t1 both heights7m, at t4 both10m. Each pair is checked in both original equations.

The parabola peaks at t3 with height H(3)=−9+18+2=11m. Ground time solves −t²+6t+2=0, giving t=3±√11; only positive t≈6.317s belongs to post-release time. The line at t3 is9m. A horizontal reference y=8 also crosses H at t=3±√3, two additional independent exact target solutions.

The publisher culminating source has two substantial open tasks (a quadratic height model and a parabola–line intersection) and offers a choice of presentation/gallery walk. This first-party adaptation deliberately uses other equations H(t)=-t^2+6t+2 and P(t)=t+6 while retaining independent problem selection, two-task structure, physical domain, and exact intersection reasoning; no source screenshot or publisher graph is copied.

Student culminating task — choose and independently solve two substantial ORIGINAL contexts without prescribed algebraic method. Task A: analyze the hypothetical H(t)=-t^2+6t+2 flight: initial height, maximum height/time, first nonnegative time reaching ground, and the two nonnegative times at height 8m; justify the useful equation form. Task B: analyze the line P(t)=t+6 and parabola H(t) on the same coordinate plane, derive all equal-height intersections algebraically and graphically, and explain why equal heights cannot establish a collision without horizontal-position data. Learners may complete both tasks or, if teacher authorizes, select one and prepare a visual display with a group/gallery-walk discussion. No graphing tool is required, but record genuine use if chosen. Original-first-party numbers are NOT publisher task/figure copies. Human-review draft rubric: 0–2 each for independently selected equivalent quadratic forms, exact verified solutions and units, complete labeled graph and contextual interpretation, and critique of model assumptions and clear group presentation. This task is human scored; generated examples, static SVGs and a rubric JSON never constitute a submitted assignment or a persisted grade.

KeyConcepts.Definition: Physical flight ends at first nonnegative ground root.

KeyConcepts.Title: Model limitations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Matching height does not establish shared spatial location or actual collision.
